quote.translation: Take the poem "In my heart I do not forget you, yet the days when tamatama I do not see you are many, and the months have passed" (Man'yō, book 4).

regions.text: ）といふ場合、全體としての一年は部分として三百六十五日を含んでるる。

quote.translation: Here the year as a whole contains three hundred and sixty-five days as its parts.

regions.text: 三百六十五日を含んでるる。假

quote.translation: Suppose they met on a certain day of a certain month.

regions.text: 假りに菜月某日相見たとしたならばそれは三百六十五の部分の中の一つに雀つてゐるので、他の部分としての他の日でもあり得た可能性を有つてゐるのである。或は甲の日でも或は乙の日でも或は丙の日でも或は丁の日でもあり待たのである。

quote.translation: That day corresponds to one of the three hundred and sixty-five parts, and so it carries the possibility of having been another day, another part: it could have been day A, or day B, or day C, or day D. Yet it was, tamatama, this particular day of this particular month, and that it was so has contingency in relation to the year as a whole.

regions.text: でも或は丁の日でもあり待たのである

quote.translation: The contingent here is nothing other than disjunctive contingency.

regions.text: 然るにそれは嫌楽月菜日であつたのである。

quote.translation: Let us give a few more examples of disjunctive contingency.

regions.text: 菜月装日であつたことは全體としての一年に對して偶然性を有つてある。その偶然とは離接前偶然にほかならない。

quote.translation: "Though wakuraba ni I am human, though I too have been made like other men, on my shoulders I throw only rags, a sleeveless jacket of cloth without cotton padding, hanging in tatters like sea-pine, ......

regions.text: 離接的偶然の例をなほ少し暴げて見よう。

quote.translation: Is it so helpless as this, the way of the world?"

regions.text: 一かくらばご人とはあるを人覚に吾も儲るを綿も無き布肩衣の、海松のごとわわけさがれる檻機のみ肩に打ち懸け、.…斯くばかり術なきものか、世の中の道』（必葉巻五）。

quote.translation: That wakuraba ni here means disjunctive contingency becomes clear if we compare it with a poem such as "If only I can be merry in this world, in the life to come I would gladly become an insect or a bird" (Man'yō, book 3).

regions.text: この場合の「わくらばに」が離接的偶然を意味してるることは「この世にし楽しくあらば來む生には蟲に鳥にも吾はなりなむ』（営葉参三）などと比較すれば明腹である。「だだこの念佛門は、かへすがへすも他の心なく後世を思はんともがらの、よしなき解胤にを

quote.translation: Or again: "This nembutsu gate is spoken solely for those people who, though they are companions who should think of the life to come again and again with no other mind, turn to pointless mistaken causes, practise miscellaneous practices without regard to the time or to themselves, and, though this time they were tamatama born into the human realm so hard to receive, throw away the vow of Amida so hard to meet, return again to the old home of the three evil paths, turn through the wheel of birth and death, and do not know the sorrow of passing many hundreds of thousands of kalpas" (Wago tōroku, Nenbutsu taii).
